claims.text: The solutions of simultaneous equations are the values of the unknown variables which satisfy both equations simultaneously.

items.stem: Solve for $x$ and $y$ : $\begin{align*}x-y&=1\qquad\ldots(1)\\3&=y-2x\qquad\ldots(2)\end{align*}$
solution: Use equation to express in terms of: $x=y+1$
Substitute into equation and solve for: $\begin{align*}3&=y-2\left(y+1\right)\\3&=y-2y-2\\5&=-y\\\therefore y&=-5\end{align*}$
Substitute back into equation and solve for: $\begin{align*}x&=(-5)+1\\\thereforex&=-4\end{align*}$

items.stem: Solve the following system of equations: $\begin{align*}4y+3x&=100\qquad\ldots(1)\\4y-19x&=12\qquad\ldots(2)\end{align*}$
solution: Use either equation to express in terms of: $\begin{align*}4y+3x&=100\\3x&=100-4y\\x&=\frac{100-4y}{3}\end{align*}$
Substitute into equation and solve for: $\begin{align*}4y-19\left(\frac{100-4y}{3}\right)&=12\\12y-19\left(100-4y\right)&=36\\12y-\text{1900}+76y&=36\\88y&=\text{1936}\\\therefore y&=22\end{align*}$
Substitute back into equation and solve for: $\begin{align*}x&=\frac{100-4\left(22\right)}{3}\\&=\frac{100-88}{3}\\&=\frac{12}{3}\\\thereforex&=4\end{align*}$

items.stem: Solve the following system of equations: $\begin{align*}3x+y&=2\qquad\ldots(1)\\6x-y&=25\qquad\ldots(2)\end{align*}$
solution: Make the coefficients of one of the variables the same in both equations: The coefficients of $y$ in the given equations are $\text{1}$ and $-\text{1}$ . Eliminate the variable $y$ by adding equation $\left(1\right)$ and equation $\left(2\right)$ together: $\begin{align*}\begin{array}{cccc}&3x+y&=&2\\+&6x-y&=&25\\\hline&9x+0&=&27\end{array}\end{align*}$
Substitute back into either original equation and solve for: $\begin{align*}3\left(3\right)+y&=2\\y&=2-9\\\therefore y&=-7\end{align*}$

items.stem: Solve for $x$ and $y$ : $y=\frac{2(x^{2}+2)-3}{x^{2}+2}$ and $y=2-\dfrac{3}{x^2+2}$
solution: Since this is true for all $x$ in the real numbers, $x$ can be any real number. Look at what happens to $y$ when $x$ is very small or very large: The smallest $x$ can be is 0. When $x=0$ , $y=2-\frac{3}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$ . If $x$ gets very large, then the fraction $\dfrac{3}{x^{2}+2}$ becomes very small (think about what happens when you divide a small number by a very large number). Then $y=2-0=2$ . From this we can see that $\frac{1}{2}\leqy\leq2$ . Therefore $x$ can be any real number, $\frac{1}{2}\leqy<2$ .
items.printed_answer: x can be any real number, 1 2 ≤ y < 2
items.blind_answer: The two equations are identical, so there are infinitely many solutions: y=2-\dfrac{3}{x^{2}+2} for every real x (no unique solution).
